mainTopic: Which fire and spices qualify for the ברכות of הבדלה: a flame that 'rested', flames of a גוי, fire and scents of unknown source, and fire or spices not used for light or fragrance
overview: This amud is about which fire and which spices may be used for the ברכות of הבדלה. First the גמרא defines a נר ששבת: a flame is disqualified only if it was tied to forbidden work (מלאכת עבירה) on שבת, not if it was used for a permitted need like a חולה. Next it explains why a Jew may bless on a flame lit from a גוי's fire but not on one a גוי lit from a גוי. The Jew blesses on the permitted addition, and the גוי-from-גוי case is banned by a גזירה. Then come cases of fire seen outside a city: follow the town's majority, check a child holding a torch, and require a fire as big as a furnace opening. A series of contradictions about furnace, oven, and בית הכנסת lights all resolve the same way: you bless only on fire whose light is actually being used. After a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל on whether a group blesses together, the גמרא explains the משנה that the candle and spices of the dead get no ברכה. It ends with rules for spices: no ברכה on a scent not made to be smelled, and choosing to smell the incense of עבודה זרה is a sin.

steps.title: Does 'did not rest' mean any work at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests one meaning of 'did not rest' and knocks it down with a ברייתא about fire lit for a חיה or a חולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say 'did not rest' means the flame was used for any work, even permitted work, that is a problem. A ברייתא teaches that we may bless on a fire lit on שבת for a woman giving birth or a sick person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that a flame 'did not rest' if it was used for any kind of work on שבת, even permitted work. It then immediately challenges this from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fire lit on שבת for a חיה or a dangerously ill חולה was lit for work that is fully permitted. If any work at all disqualified a flame, we could not bless on this fire. But the ברייתא says we may bless on it, so 'did not rest' cannot mean any work at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If we say: the גמרא is proposing a possible explanation in order to test it
Permitted work: work allowed on שבת, such as saving a life
But it was taught in a ברייתא: introduces a source that contradicts the proposal
A woman in childbirth, for whom we may break שבת
A sick person (here, one in danger), for whom we may break שבת

steps.confusionAlert: In this context, חיה does not mean an animal. It means a woman giving birth.

phrases.english: If we say 'it did not rest' means
phrases.notes: Refers to the rule that we do not bless on a flame that did not rest on שבת

phrases.english: because of labor
phrases.notes: Meaning the flame was used for work

phrases.english: even from permitted labor,
but wasn't it taught in a baraita:
fire of a woman giving birth or of a sick person —
phrases.notes: Fire lit on שבת for their needs

phrases.english: we bless over it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא לֹא שָׁבַת מֵחֲמַת מְלָאכָה אֲפִילּוּ מִמְּלָאכָה דְּהֶתֵּירָא, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the previous daf, where the גמרא asked what 'לא שבת' means
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that any work, even permitted work, makes a flame 'not rested'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fire lit for a חיה or a חולה was used for permitted work, yet the ברייתא allows blessing on it. So permitted work cannot disqualify a flame.

steps.title: 'Rested' means rested from forbidden work
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'rested' means the flame was not used for a forbidden act on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What does 'rested' mean? It means the flame rested from forbidden work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the correct meaning of 'rested'. Only a flame used for a sin on שבת is disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the rule. A flame lit for a permitted reason, like for a חולה, is fine. A flame that simply kept burning all of שבת is also fine. Only a fire lit or used in violation of שבת cannot be used for הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: What does 'rested' mean? The term is being defined
Work of transgression: forbidden work done in violation of שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the working definition for the rest of the sugya. The disqualification comes from a flame tied to a שבת violation, not from mere use.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
what is meant by 'rested'? —
that it rested from labor of transgression.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי ״שָׁבַת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by redefining the term
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Rested' meant the flame was not used for any work at all
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Rested' means not used for forbidden work, so fire lit for a חיה or a חולה is valid

steps.title: Support: a lamp that burned all of שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about a lamp burning all of שבת supports רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: a lamp that kept burning the entire day of שבת may be used for the blessing after שבת ends.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamp that burned all of שבת did not literally 'rest', because it was burning and giving light the whole time. Still, we may bless on it, since nothing forbidden was done with it. This shows that 'rested' means free of forbidden work, just as רב נחמן בר יצחק said.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way: introduces a ברייתא that supports what was just said

steps.whatToRemember: A flame is valid for הבדלה unless it was connected to a שבת violation. Fire for a חולה or a חיה, and a lamp that burned all of שבת, are both valid.

phrases.english: It was also taught so in a baraita:
a lantern that was continuously burning
the entire day,
at the conclusion of Shabbat we bless over it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 2
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's definition: 'rested' means rested from forbidden work
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a lamp that burned all of שבת is valid for הבדלה

steps.title: Flames passed between a גוי and a Jew
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא rules on flames lit by a גוי and a Jew from each other's fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if a גוי lit a flame from a Jew's fire, or a Jew lit a flame from a גוי's fire, we bless on it. If a גוי lit from a גוי's fire, we do not bless on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about who lit the flame and whose fire it came from. This sets up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases are valid: a גוי lighting from a Jew, and a Jew lighting from a גוי. Only a גוי lighting from a גוי is invalid. The ברייתא does not give its reason, so the גמרא will try to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא
Who lit from: lit his flame from someone else's fire

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
a gentile who lit from a Jew,
and a Jew who lit from a gentile —
we bless over it.
A gentile from a gentile —
we do not bless over it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גּוֹי שֶׁהִדְלִיק מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic within the laws of the הבדלה flame
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A flame lit by a גוי from a Jew, or by a Jew from a גוי, is valid for הבדלה. A flame lit by a גוי from a גוי is not.

steps.title: Why is a גוי lighting from a גוי invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ברייתא and suggests the flame 'did not rest'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a flame a גוי lit from a גוי, that we do not bless on it? Is it because it did not rest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא disqualifies the case of a גוי lighting from a גוי. It suggests the reason is that the flame 'did not rest'. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gentiles are not commanded to keep שבת, so a flame among gentiles was likely used for work that would be forbidden for a Jew on שבת. The suggested reason ties this case to the rule of נר שלא שבת from the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks why one case is treated differently from others

phrases.english: What is different about a gentile from a gentile that we do not bless —
because it did not rest?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא גּוֹי מִגּוֹי דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a flame lit by a גוי from a גוי is invalid for הבדלה

steps.title: Then a Jew lighting from a גוי should also be invalid
steps.stepSummary: The suggested reason fails, because a Jew's flame lit from a גוי's fire also comes from a fire that did not rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a flame a Jew lit from a גוי also did not rest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason it just suggested. If 'did not rest' were the reason, the ברייתא should also disqualify a Jew lighting from a גוי, but it allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of a Jew lighting from a גוי, the source fire is still the גוי's fire that did not rest. Lighting a new flame from it should not fix that problem. Yet the ברייתא permits it, so 'did not rest' cannot explain the distinction, and the גמרא needs a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge based on the reason just suggested
But: here it points out what follows from the suggested reason

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not saying a Jew lighting from a גוי is really invalid. It shows that the suggested reason does not fit the ברייתא, so another explanation is needed.

phrases.english: If so,
a Jew who lit from a gentile also —
it did not rest!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, יִשְׂרָאֵל מִגּוֹי נָמֵי הָא לֹא שָׁבַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason suggested in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that a גוי lighting from a גוי is invalid because the flame did not rest
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Jew lighting from a גוי also takes from a flame that did not rest, yet the ברייתא permits it. So the suggested reason cannot be what separates the two cases.

steps.title: Suggestion: the Jew's flame is a brand-new flame
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the forbidden flame is gone, and a new flame was born in the Jew's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: that forbidden flame is gone, and this is a different flame, which is being born in the hand of a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out of the problem from Step 6, explaining why a Jew's flame lit from a גוי's fire is fine. This suggestion is set up only so it can be tested and rejected in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire keeps renewing itself, so maybe the flame in the Jew's candle is not the same 'thing' as the גוי's forbidden flame. If so, the Jew's flame never had the problem of 'not resting' (לא שבת). This would explain why a Jew lighting from a גוי gets a blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer)
The forbidden one (the flame with the problem)
It is born / comes into being

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the גמרא's final answer. The phrase וכי תימא introduces an idea that the גמרא will immediately knock down.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הַךְ אִיסּוּרָא אֲזַל לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And if you will say: that forbidden flame has gone away,
and this one is a different flame,
phrases.notes: A flame constantly renews itself.

phrases.english: and it is being born in the hand of a Jew —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הַךְ אִיסּוּרָא אֲזַל לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a defense against the difficulty raised in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the object: the flame is a new entity each moment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A Jew's flame lit from a גוי's fire seems to come from a fire that did not rest, so it should not get a blessing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden flame is gone; the Jew's flame is a new flame, so it has no problem.

steps.title: Rejection: carrying a flame on שבת proves it is one object
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails, because a ברייתא says one who carries a flame into the public domain is חייב, which only makes sense if the flame stays the same object.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about that which was taught: One who carries a flame out into the public domain is liable. Why is he liable? What he picked up, he did not put down, and what he put down, he did not pick up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea from Step 7 by quoting a ברייתא about carrying (הוצאה) on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be חייב for carrying, a person must pick up (עקירה) and put down (הנחה) the SAME object. If a flame were a new flame every moment, the flame he put down would not be the one he picked up, and he would not be חייב. Since the ברייתא says he IS חייב, a flame must count as one continuing object, so the forbidden flame is not 'gone.'

keyTerms.meaning: But what about this that was taught (introduces a source that contradicts)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that in הלכה a flame is treated as one continuing thing, not something re-created each moment.

phrases.english: But what about that which was taught:
One who carries a flame out to the public domain is liable.
phrases.notes: Liable for the מלאכה of carrying on שבת.

phrases.english: Why is he liable?
What he picked up, he did not put down,
and what he put down, he did not pick up!
phrases.notes: This would be true if a flame were new every moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the suggestion of Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea that a flame is a new object each moment.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts the ruling that one who carries a flame on שבת is חייב, which requires the same object to be picked up and put down.

steps.title: The blessing is on the permitted addition to the flame
steps.stepSummary: The forbidden flame is really still there, but the Jew blesses on the new, permitted part of the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, actually the forbidden flame is also still there, and when he says the blessing, he says the blessing on the permitted addition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the problem from Step 6, after the first answer was rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא now admits the forbidden flame still exists. But when the Jew lights his candle after שבת, new fire is added, and that added part never had any problem. The blessing goes on that permitted addition (תוספתא דהתירא).

phrases.english: Rather, actually the forbidden flame is also still there,
and when he recites the blessing —
he recites the blessing on the permitted addition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיסּוּרָא נָמֵי אִיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 7 with a new answer to Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifting the object of the blessing from the whole flame to the added part.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Jew's flame contains forbidden fire, so no blessing should be possible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden fire is there, but the blessing is on the permitted new addition.

steps.title: Then a גוי lighting from a גוי should also work
steps.stepSummary: If the blessing is on the permitted addition, then a flame a גוי lit from a גוי should also get a blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a גוי lighting from a גוי too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 9 by showing it seems to prove too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second גוי lighting from the first גוי's flame after שבת also creates a permitted addition. So by the logic of Step 9, we should bless on it too. But the ברייתא from Step 4 says we do NOT bless on a flame a גוי lit from a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge from the previous logic)
A גוי lighting from a גוי's flame

phrases.english: If so, a gentile lighting from a gentile too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, גּוֹי מִגּוֹי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That answer would also permit a blessing on a גוי-from-גוי flame, which contradicts the ברייתא in Step 4.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree because of the first גוי and first flame
steps.stepSummary: Yes, in principle it should work, but the חכמים forbade it because of the first גוי and the original flame lit on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so; it is a decree because of the first גוי and the first pillar of flame.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of Step 10 by admitting the logic, but explaining that the חכמים made a גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By pure logic, a גוי-from-גוי flame has a permitted addition. But people might confuse it with the first גוי's flame, or the original flame lit on שבת itself, which have no permitted addition. So the חכמים forbade blessing on any flame of a גוי lit from a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (the גמרא agrees with the challenge's logic)
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
The first 'pillar' (the original flame lit on שבת)

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew's flame from a גוי gets a blessing because of the permitted addition. A גוי's flame from a גוי has the same logic, but the חכמים forbade it with a גזירה because of the first גוי and the original flame.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does NOT say a גוי-from-גוי flame lacks a permitted addition. It agrees it has one; the ban is only a rabbinic גזירה.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם גּוֹי רִאשׁוֹן וְעַמּוּד רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: it is a decree because of the first gentile and the first pillar of flame.
phrases.notes: The first גוי and the first flame were lit on שבת itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין הָכִי נָמֵי, גְּזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees with the logic but adds a rabbinic decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי-from-גוי flame should get a blessing because of its permitted addition.
steps.terutzMaskana: It would, but the חכמים forbade it as a גזירה because of the first גוי and the first flame.

steps.title: Fire seen outside a city: follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if one sees fire outside a city, he blesses only if most of the city's people are Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: If he was walking outside the city and saw fire, if most are גוים he does not bless; if most are Jews he blesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about blessing on a fire when you do not know who lit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the source of the fire is unknown, we assume it follows the majority of the people living there. If most are גוים, the fire is likely from a גוי and may not be blessed on. If most are Jews, it is likely a Jew's fire and may be blessed on.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ חוּץ לַכְּרַךְ וְרָאָה אוּר,
phrases.english: If he was walking outside the city and saw fire,
if the majority are gentiles, he does not recite the blessing;
if the majority are Jews, he recites the blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ חוּץ לַכְּרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ruling about fire of unknown source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the source of a fire is unknown, follow the majority of the city: majority גוים means no blessing; majority Jews means a blessing.

steps.title: The two halves of the ברייתא seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא's two clauses lead to opposite rulings for a city that is half Jews and half גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא contradicts itself. You said that if most people are גוים, he does not bless. That suggests that half-and-half, he does bless. Then you teach that if most are Jews, he blesses. That suggests that half-and-half, he does not bless!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא from Step 12 carefully and finds an internal contradiction about a city that is exactly half Jews and half גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause blocks the ברכה only when most are גוים, so a 50/50 city should be fine. The second clause allows the ברכה only when most are Jews, so a 50/50 city should not be fine. The same ברייתא cannot imply both rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: This text itself is difficult (it contradicts itself)

steps.confusionAlert: Neither clause actually mentions a half-and-half city. Both 'rulings' about 50/50 are inferences (דיוקים) drawn from what each clause leaves out.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא says a teaching seems to contradict itself.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ אִם רוֹב גּוֹיִם — אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ,
phrases.english: You said: if most are gentiles, he does not bless,
which implies that half-and-half, he does bless,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי אִם רוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל — מְבָרֵךְ,
phrases.english: and then it teaches: if most are Jews, he blesses,

phrases.aramaic: הָא מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה — אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ!
phrases.english: which implies that half-and-half, he does not bless!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גוּפָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא quoted in Step 12 from within
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא about seeing fire outside a city
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The inference from the רישא contradicts the inference from the סיפא in the 50/50 case

steps.title: A half-and-half city does get a ברכה; the wording just matches
steps.stepSummary: The real law is that a 50/50 city gets a ברכה. The סיפא says 'most Jews' only to parallel the רישא's 'most גוים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: By right, even half-and-half he blesses. But since the first clause taught 'most גוים', the last clause taught 'most Jews'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by siding with the first clause. It explains the second clause as a style choice, not a precise ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference from the רישא is the real law: a 50/50 city gets a ברכה. The סיפא's phrase 'most Jews' should not be read too exactly. It was used only to keep the wording parallel, a known style called איידי.

keyTerms.meaning: By right / according to the true law
Since (it said X, it also said Y); wording chosen for parallelism

steps.whatToRemember: Seeing fire outside a city: one blesses unless most of the city are גוים, so a 50/50 city gets a ברכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common tool: a clause's wording may come from matching the other clause, so we do not draw a דיוק from it.

phrases.english: By right, even
half-and-half, he also blesses,
but since the first clause taught 'most gentiles',
the last clause taught 'most Jews'.
phrases.notes: That's just how it's phrased, not an exact rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדִין הוּא דַּאֲפִילּוּ מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה נָמֵי מְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism (איידי): one clause's wording is not meant precisely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses carry exact meaning, so the 50/50 case is contradictory
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא sets the law (50/50 gets a ברכה); the סיפא's wording is for parallelism

steps.title: A child carrying a torch: check who he is
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: if one sees a child with a torch outside the city, he must check whether the child is Jewish. If so, he blesses; if not, he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Someone walking outside the city sees a child holding a torch. He checks into the child's background. If the child is a Jew, he blesses. If he is a גוי, he does not bless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about seeing a torch, not a whole city's fire. It rules that one must find out who is holding the torch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the fire is in a specific person's hand, so instead of relying on the town's majority (as in Step 12), one can check that person directly. A Jew's torch was likely lit properly after שבת and gets a ברכה. A גוי's torch may come from a flame lit on שבת, which was disqualified earlier.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ חוּץ לַכְּרַךְ
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: If one was walking outside the city
and saw a child with a torch in his hand,
he checks into who he is;
if he is a Jew, he blesses;
if he is a gentile, he does not bless.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ חוּץ לַכְּרַךְ וְרָאָה תִּינוֹק וַאֲבוּקָה בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a city's fire to an individual's torch, using the same Jew/גוי principle
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A torch held by a Jewish child gets a ברכה; one held by a non-Jewish child does not, so one must check first

steps.title: Why mention a child? An adult needs the same check
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's wording: an adult with a torch would also need to be checked, so why specify a child?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it say specifically a child? Even an adult would need checking too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why the ברייתא chose the case of a child. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The check depends on whether the torch-holder is Jewish, and that applies equally to adults. So the word 'child' looks unnecessary. The גמרא expects there must be a special reason for it.

phrases.english: Why specifically a child?
Even an adult as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא תִּינוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the specific case chosen in the ברייתא of Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's choice of a 'child' holding the torch
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The deciding factor is Jew versus גוי, which applies equally to adults, so 'child' seems unnecessary

steps.title: The case is right after sunset, so an adult is obviously a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, answers why the ברייתא mentions a child. The case is just after sunset on מוצאי שבת. An adult holding fire that early is clearly a נכרי. A child might be a Jew who just happened to pick up the torch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: We are dealing with a time right after sunset. With an adult, it is clear that he must be a non-Jew. With a child, you could say he is a Jew who just happened to take the torch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16, which asked why the ברייתא says 'a child' when an adult would also need checking. רב says the case is so soon after שבת ended that an adult does not need checking at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after שבת ends, a Jewish adult would not already be walking around with fire. So an adult with a torch is surely a נכרי, and you do not bless over his fire. A child is less careful, so he might be Jewish. That is why only a child needs to be checked.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to sunset, meaning just after שבת has ended
We are dealing with (a specific case)
The matter is obvious and proves itself
It just happened that he took it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא means adults never need checking at any time. This answer only works because the case is right after sunset. At a later hour, an adult would also need to be checked.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Here we are dealing with a time close to sunset.
phrases.notes: Sunset at the end of שבת

phrases.english: With an adult, the matter is obvious
that he is certainly a non-Jew.
phrases.notes: A Jewish adult would not have fire in hand so soon after שבת

phrases.english: With a child, say that he is a Jew,
who just happened to take it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הָכָא בְּסָמוּךְ לִשְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge from step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a specific time (right after sunset)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An adult should need checking just like a child, so mentioning 'child' seems pointless
steps.terutzMaskana: Right after sunset, an adult is surely a נכרי, so only a child is uncertain and needs checking

steps.title: A fire as thick as a furnace opening gets a blessing
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that someone walking outside a city who sees a fire may bless over it if the fire is as thick as a furnace opening. If it is not that thick, he does not bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone was walking outside the city and saw a fire, he blesses over it if it is as thick as the opening of a furnace. If not, he does not bless over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about seeing a fire outside the city at הבדלה time. It gives a size test: a big, thick fire gets a ברכה, and a small one does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fire that large is made to give light as well, so it is fit for the ברכה on fire. A small fire outside the city does not show that it is a light-giving fire, so no ברכה is said. This ruling also sets up the next step, which deals with furnace fire.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ חוּץ לַכְּרַךְ
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: If one was walking outside the city
and saw a fire,
if it is as thick as the opening of a furnace,
he blesses over it.
And if not, he does not bless over it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ חוּץ לַכְּרַךְ וְרָאָה אוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ברייתא about the size of a fire seen outside the city
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fire seen outside the city gets a ברכה only if it is as thick as a furnace opening

steps.title: Two teachings disagree about blessing on furnace fire
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says we bless over a furnace's fire. Another ברייתא says we do not. The גמרא points out the contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: We bless over the fire of a furnace. Another ברייתא teaches: We do not bless over it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two ברייתות side by side that seem to contradict each other about furnace fire. It is setting up a resolution in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources talk about the same kind of fire, a furnace fire, yet they give opposite rulings. Both cannot be correct as stated, so the גמרא will need to show that they are talking about different situations.

phrases.english: One ברייתא teaches:
We bless over the fire of a furnace,
and another ברייתא teaches:
We do not bless over it!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: אוּר שֶׁל כִּבְשָׁן מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: אֵין מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the furnace topic by showing two sources that contradict each other
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about furnace fire
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give opposite rulings about the same fire

steps.title: No blessing at the start of the furnace, but yes at the end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The ברייתא that forbids a ברכה is talking about the beginning, when the fire only heats the furnace. The one that allows a ברכה is talking about the end, when the fire's light is used.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: This one is at the beginning, and that one is at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different stage of the furnace's use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a furnace is first lit, the fire is there only to heat what is inside, not to give light, so we do not bless. Later, once the heating is no longer needed, the fire's light gets used, so we bless. What matters is whether the fire is serving as light.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources can both be true

steps.whatToRemember: For the ברכה on fire at הבדלה, the fire must be serving as light. A furnace fire made only for heat does not count at first. Later, when its light is used, it does count.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule for the הבדלה fire blessing: what decides it is the fire's purpose, not the fire itself.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is at the beginning,
phrases.notes: No ברכה: the fire is only for heating

phrases.english: that one is at the end.
phrases.notes: ברכה: the fire's light is now being used

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בַּתְּחִלָּה, הָא לְבַסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases by time (each source talks about a different stage)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות truly disagree about furnace fire
steps.terutzMaskana: At the start the fire is only for heat, so no ברכה. At the end its light is used, so a ברכה is said.

steps.title: Two teachings disagree about blessing over an oven or stove fire
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says we may bless over the fire of a תנור or כירים at הבדלה. Another ברייתא says we may not. The גמרא points out the contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: we bless over the fire of an oven or a stove. Another ברייתא teaches: we do not bless over it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second pair of ברייתות that clash, this time about an oven or stove fire. This is a new contradiction, set up like the furnace one in Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling being challenged is about the ברכה over fire at הבדלה (בורא מאורי האש). One source allows it over a cooking fire and the other forbids it. Both cannot be true as they stand, so the גמרא needs a way to divide the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: "One [ברייתא] teaches": opens the first of two sources
"And another [ברייתא] teaches": brings the source that disagrees

phrases.english: One [ברייתא] teaches: the fire of an oven
phrases.notes: The context is the ברכה over fire at הבדלה.

phrases.english: and of a stove, we bless over it,
and another [ברייתא] teaches: we do not bless over it!
phrases.notes: The exclamation mark shows the גמרא sees a contradiction here.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא אוּר שֶׁל תַּנּוּר וְשֶׁל כִּירַיִם מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ אֵין מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel contradiction to the furnace case in Steps 19–20, now about an oven and stove.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about blessing over an oven or stove fire
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Direct contradiction: one source permits the ברכה and the other forbids it for the same kind of fire.

steps.title: Beginning versus end of the oven's use
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that forbids the ברכה is talking about the beginning, when the fire is lit to cook. The one that permits it is talking about the end, when the fire's light is being used.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one [which forbids] is at the beginning. That one [which permits] is at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction the same way it settled the furnace case. It splits the two ברייתות by timing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the beginning, the fire is there only to heat the food, so it does not count as a light to bless over. Later, when the cooking is done and people use the fire for its light, a ברכה is allowed. The type of fire stays the same; only its purpose changes.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is not difficult": the formula that opens an answer
At the beginning, when the fire is lit for cooking
At the end, when the fire's light is used

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the guiding rule of this section. A fire qualifies for the ברכה when it is serving as light, not because of what kind of fire it is.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is at the beginning, that one is at the end.
phrases.notes: Beginning goes with the ברייתא that forbids (the fire is for heating). End goes with the one that permits (the fire is for light).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא בַּתְּחִלָּה הָא לְבַסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in Step 21 using the same split as Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא refers to a different stage of the fire's use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seem to rule differently about the very same oven fire.
steps.terutzMaskana: Early on, the fire is only for cooking, so there is no ברכה. Later, its light is used, so a ברכה is allowed.

steps.title: Two teachings disagree about blessing over the light in a synagogue or study hall
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא allows a ברכה at הבדלה over the light of a בית הכנסת or בית המדרש. Another ברייתא forbids it. The גמרא points out the contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: we bless over the light of a synagogue or a study hall. Another ברייתא teaches: we do not bless over it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third pair of clashing ברייתות, now about lights in a בית הכנסת or בית המדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question here is not cooking versus light. These are lamps in holy places. One source allows blessing over them and the other forbids it, so the גמרא needs a new way to divide the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: "We bless over it": here, the ברכה over fire at הבדלה

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: אוּר שֶׁל בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת
phrases.english: One [ברייתא] teaches: the light of a synagogue
and of a study hall, we bless over it,
and another [ברייתא] teaches: we do not bless over it!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא אוּר שֶׁל בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת וְשֶׁל בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ אֵין מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another contradiction in the same series, moving from cooking fires to the lights of holy places.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about the light in a בית הכנסת or בית המדרש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Direct contradiction: one source permits the ברכה and the other forbids it for the same lights.

steps.title: It depends on whether an important person is present
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that forbids the ברכה is talking about a case where an אדם חשוב is there, so the light was lit in his honor. The one that permits it is talking about a case with no אדם חשוב, so the light was lit to see by.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one [which forbids] is where there is an important person. That one [which permits] is where there is no important person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases based on who is present. This is the first of three answers to this contradiction; Steps 25 and 26 offer alternatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an important person is there, the lights are lit to honor him, not to give light. So they are like the oven fire that is only for cooking, and there is no ברכה. When no such person is there, the lights are lit to see by, so a ברכה is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: An important or distinguished person, such as a leading scholar

steps.confusionAlert: Do not flip the matching. "There is an important person" goes with the ברייתא that FORBIDS the ברכה, because the light is for honor. "There is no important person" goes with the one that PERMITS it.
steps.whatToRemember: All three contradictions (furnace, oven and stove, synagogue) are solved with the same idea. You bless over fire only when it is serving as light. If it is lit for heat or for honor, there is no ברכה.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where there is an important person,
phrases.notes: This goes with the ברייתא that forbids: the light is lit in his honor.

phrases.english: that one is where there is no important person.
phrases.notes: This goes with the ברייתא that permits: the light is lit for seeing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא דְּאִיכָּא אָדָם חָשׁוּב הָא דְּלֵיכָּא אָדָם חָשׁוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא refers to a different situation, based on why the light was lit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seem to give opposite rulings about the same synagogue lights.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the light is lit to honor an אדם חשוב, there is no ברכה. When it is lit to see by, a ברכה is allowed.

steps.title: Second answer: a caretaker who uses the light
steps.stepSummary: Both ברייתות may be talking about a case where an אדם חשוב is present. The difference is whether there is a חזנא who uses the light.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say that both ברייתות are talking about a case where an important person is there. It is still not a contradiction. One ברייתא is talking about a case where there is a caretaker, and the other is talking about a case where there is no caretaker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the same contradiction from step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when an אדם חשוב is there, a חזנא who uses the light for his work makes it a light that is used for seeing, so you may bless on it. With no חזנא, the light is only there for honor, so you may not bless on it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: this introduces another possible answer
This one and that one: both ברייתות
The caretaker or attendant of the בית הכנסת
And it is not difficult: there is no real contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: Here חזנא means the בית הכנסת caretaker. It does not mean the חזן who leads תפילה.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say
this and that are where there is an important person,
and it is not difficult:
this one is where there is a caretaker,
phrases.notes: He uses the light, so you may bless on it.

phrases.english: that one is where there is no caretaker.
phrases.notes: The light is only for honor, so you may not bless on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא הָא וְהָא דְּאִיכָּא אָדָם חָשׁוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different resolution to the contradiction from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): both ברייתות are placed in a case with an אדם חשוב, and the difference is whether a caretaker is present.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The presence of an אדם חשוב might seem to always mean the light is for honor only.
steps.terutzMaskana: A caretaker who uses the light makes it a light for seeing, even when an אדם חשוב is there.

steps.title: Third answer: whether there is moonlight
steps.stepSummary: Both ברייתות may be talking about a case with a חזנא. The difference is whether there is moonlight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say that both ברייתות are talking about a case where there is a caretaker. It is still not a contradiction. One ברייתא is talking about a case where there is moonlight, and the other is talking about a case where there is no moonlight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer to the same contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is moonlight, the caretaker does not need the fire to see, so the light is not for seeing and you may not bless on it. With no moonlight, he lights it to see by, so you may bless on it.
steps.whatToRemember: The basic rule behind all these answers is this: you only bless on a fire whose light is actually being used for seeing, not a fire lit only for honor or heat.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say
this and that are where there is a caretaker,
and it is not difficult:
this one is where there is moonlight,
phrases.notes: The fire is not needed for seeing, so no ברכה.

phrases.english: and that one is where there is no moonlight.
phrases.notes: The fire is lit for seeing, so a ברכה is said.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא הָא וְהָא דְּאִיכָּא חַזָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third resolution. It builds on the caretaker case from step 25 and narrows it further.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): both ברייתות are placed in a case with a caretaker, and the difference is moonlight.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A caretaker might seem to always mean the light is used for seeing.
steps.terutzMaskana: If moonlight is enough to see by, the fire is not needed for light, so you do not bless on it.

steps.title: Should each person bless on the fire, or one for everyone?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a מחלוקת. When fire is brought before a group in the בית המדרש, בית שמאי say each person blesses alone, and בית הלל say one blesses for all because ברב עם הדרת מלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: People were sitting in the בית המדרש and fire was brought in front of them. בית שמאי say: each person makes the ברכה for himself. בית הלל say: one person makes the ברכה for everyone, because the פסוק says, 'The King's glory is in a large crowd of people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings a ברייתא about how a group in the בית המדרש makes the ברכה on fire at הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל hold that one person making the ברכה while everyone answers אמן gives more honor to השם, because a big group praises Him together. בית שמאי hold that each person should bless on his own. The ברייתא gives בית הלל's reason but not בית שמאי's.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: this introduces a ברייתא
The King's glory is in a multitude of people (משלי י״ד:כ״ח)

steps.whyThisMatters: ברב עם הדרת מלך is a well-known principle in הלכה. It is the reason why one person often makes a ברכה for a whole group.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
They were sitting in the study hall
and they brought fire before them,
Beit Shammai say:
each and every one blesses for himself.
And Beit Hillel say:
one blesses for all of them,
because it is stated:
"In the multitude of people is the King's glory."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ יוֹשְׁבִין בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It moves from which fire you may bless on to how a group makes the ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: each person blesses for himself. בית הלל: one blesses for everyone, because of ברב עם הדרת מלך.

steps.title: What is בית שמאי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל gave a reason for their view. The גמרא asks what בית שמאי's reason is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for בית הלל, because they explain their reason. But what is בית שמאי's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. It wants to know the reason behind בית שמאי's view, and it sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a פסוק for בית הלל but no reason for בית שמאי. The גמרא is not attacking בית שמאי. It is only asking what their logic is.

phrases.english: Granted, Beit Hillel explain the reason,
but Beit Shammai, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית הִלֵּל מְפָרְשִׁי טַעְמָא, אֶלָּא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason missing from the ברייתא in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind בית שמאי's view that each person blesses on his own.

steps.title: בית שמאי worry about interrupting learning
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold that each person blesses on his own so that learning in the בית המדרש is not interrupted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They hold this because of ביטול בית המדרש, the stopping of learning in the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question and explains בית שמאי's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone had to stop and gather to hear one person's ברכה, learning would be paused. If each person blesses quietly on his own, everyone keeps learning. So בית שמאי choose not interrupting תורה learning over the honor of a large group.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold, they are of the opinion
Interruption of learning in the study hall

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל say one person blesses for all, for the honor of השם (ברב עם הדרת מלך). בית שמאי say each person blesses alone, so learning is not interrupted (ביטול בית המדרש).

phrases.english: They hold: because of the interruption of the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבְרִי מִפְּנֵי בִּיטּוּל בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי worry that gathering everyone for one ברכה would interrupt תורה learning in the בית המדרש.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's household did not say מרפא in the בית המדרש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports בית שמאי's reason. In the house of רבן גמליאל they did not say 'מרפא' (bless you) in the בית המדרש, so as not to interrupt learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: the people of רבן גמליאל's house would not say 'healing!' (when someone sneezed) in the study hall, because it would interrupt the learning there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that 'not interrupting learning' really is a known concern. This backs up the reason just given for בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'bless you' after a sneeze is a small, polite act. Even so, רבן גמליאל's household skipped it in the בית המדרש so that learning would not stop. This shows that the worry behind בית שמאי's view, ביטול בית המדרש, was taken seriously in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (introduces a supporting ברייתא)
'Healing!' — what people said when someone sneezed, like 'bless you'
Interrupting the learning in the study hall
Head of the סנהדרין, a leading תנא

phrases.english: It was also taught like this:
The members of the house of Rabban Gamliel
would not say "healing" (after a sneeze)
in the study hall,
because of the interruption of the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reason given for בית שמאי in step 29
steps.raayaObject: בית שמאי's reason that ברכות are said individually so as not to interrupt learning in the בית המדרש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about רבן גמליאל's household not saying מרפא in the בית המדרש

steps.title: The משנה: no blessing on the candle or spices of the dead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: we do not make a ברכה on the candle or the spices of the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not make a blessing on the candle or on the spices that belong to the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up the next move, where it will ask for the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally on מוצאי שבת we make a ברכה on fire (בורא מאורי האש) and on spices (בורא מיני בשמים). The משנה says this does not apply to a candle or spices that are there for a dead person. The גמרא will now explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Belonging to / used for the dead
We do not make a blessing

phrases.english: We do not bless, neither on the candle
nor on the spices of the dead.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְבָרְכִין לֹא עַל הַנֵּר וְלֹא עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים שֶׁל מֵתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after finishing the בית שמאי / בית הלל discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ברכה is made on a candle or spices used for the dead

steps.title: Why is there no blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we do not bless on the dead's candle and spices. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A candle gives light and spices smell good, so it seems like a ברכה should be made. The גמרא wants to know what makes these different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason of the rule just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why no ברכה is made on the candle and spices of the dead

steps.title: The candle is for honor, the spices are to hide the smell
steps.stepSummary: The candle of the dead is lit to honor the dead, not for light. The spices are there to cover a bad smell, not to be enjoyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The candle is made for honor. The spices are made to get rid of the bad smell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these items are not there for us to enjoy. So there is nothing to make a ברכה on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברכה on fire or spices is for benefiting from the light or the scent. The dead's candle is lit to give honor, and the dead's spices are meant to cover a smell. Their purpose is not the kind of enjoyment the ברכה is for, so no ברכה is said.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove / cover up the (bad) smell

steps.whatToRemember: A ברכה on fire or spices depends on what they are there for. If they are for honor or for covering a smell, and not for enjoying the light or scent, no ברכה is made.

phrases.english: A candle — it is made for honor,
spices — to remove the (bad) odor
is what they are made for.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵר לְכָבוֹד הוּא דַּעֲבִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The candle is for honoring the dead and the spices are for covering the smell, not for enjoyment

steps.title: How to tell if the candle is for honor or for light
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches: if a candle is carried before the dead by day and by night, it is for honor, so no ברכה. If it is carried only at night, it is for light, so a ברכה is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: any dead person before whom a candle is taken out both by day and by night, we do not bless on it. Any dead person before whom a candle is taken out only at night, we do bless on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a practical test for whether the dead's candle is for honor or for light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A candle carried even in daytime cannot be for light, so it must be for honor, and it gets no ברכה. A candle carried only at night is clearly for light, so it gets a ברכה. This shows the משנה's rule depends on the candle's purpose, not just on the fact that it is near a dead person.

keyTerms.meaning: They take out (a candle) before him (the dead)

steps.confusionAlert: Not every candle by a dead person is off-limits for a ברכה. If it is used only at night, it is for light, and a ברכה is made.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sharpens the משנה: the rule depends on why the candle is there, not simply on it being for the dead.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Any (dead person) before whom they take out (a candle)
by day and by night —
we do not bless on it.
And any before whom they do not take out (a candle)
except at night —
we bless on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reason from step 33 (honor and not light) to a practical test
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A candle carried before the dead day and night is for honor, so no ברכה. A candle carried only at night is for light, so a ברכה is made.

steps.title: No blessing on spices or oil used to remove bad smells
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that spices in a bathroom, and oil made to remove filth, get no ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: spices of the bathroom, and oil made to remove dirt, we do not bless on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds more cases that work like the spices of the dead. They are used to remove bad smells, so no ברכה is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the reason given for the dead's spices: their job is to cover a smell, not to give enjoyment. Bathroom spices and cleaning oil have the same job, so the same rule applies.
steps.whatToRemember: A ברכה on a scent is only for a scent made to be enjoyed. Anything made just to cover a bad smell gets no ברכה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Spices of the bathroom,
and oil that is made to remove the filth —
we do not bless on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 'covering a smell' reason from step 33 to other cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bathroom spices and oil made to remove filth get no ברכה, because they are for removing smells and not for enjoyment

steps.title: Is this a general rule about smells not made for fragrance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns רב הונא's ruling into a general principle so that it can test it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that any time a scent is not made for its smell, we do not make a ברכה on it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes רב הונא's ruling and asks if it is a general rule. This is a setup line that prepares a challenge coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא gave two examples: bathroom spices and oil for removing filth. The גמרא widens them into one principle: no ברכה whenever a scent is not made for smelling. Stating it this broadly lets the גמרא test it against a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces an inference to be tested)

phrases.english: Is that to say that anywhere
that it is not made for its fragrance
we do not make a blessing over it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּכֹל הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Generalizes רב הונא's ruling into a broad principle in order to test it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether any scent not made for fragrance never gets a ברכה

steps.title: Challenge from the perfume shop
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one who smells spices in a perfume shop makes a ברכה, even though the spices are there to be sold, not to be smelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: someone who walks into a perfumer's shop and smells the scent makes only one ברכה, even if he sits there all day. If he goes in and out, again and again, he makes a ברכה each time. But here the spices are not made for smelling, since they are for sale, and still he makes a ברכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack the general rule from the last step. In a perfume shop the spices are for selling, yet a ברכה is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shopkeeper's spices are merchandise. He is not keeping them around so the room will smell good. If 'not made for fragrance means no ברכה' were true, there should be no ברכה here, but the ברייתא says there is one.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
and yet he makes a ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's details (one ברכה for staying all day, a new ברכה for each time he re-enters) are background. The real point of the challenge is only that a ברכה is made at all.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who enters the store of a perfumer
and smelled a fragrance,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יָשַׁב שָׁם כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
phrases.english: even if he sat there the entire day
he only makes a blessing once.
If he entered and left, entered and left,
he makes a blessing each and every time.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא דְּלָאו לְרֵיחָא הוּא דַּעֲבִידָא,
phrases.english: But here it is not made for fragrance,
and yet he makes a blessing!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the general principle proposed in step 36
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that a scent not made for fragrance gets no ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Perfume-shop spices are for sale, not for smelling, yet the ברייתא requires a ברכה

steps.title: The shop's smell is also made for fragrance
steps.stepSummary: The perfumer wants his shop to smell good so that people are drawn in to buy. So the scent is made for smelling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it is also made for its smell, so that people will smell it, come in, and buy from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The shop's smell really is meant to be smelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 36 stays in place. The answer changes how we see the case: the perfumer wants people to smell his spices, because the smell is his advertising. So the spices count as made for fragrance and a ברכה fits.

phrases.english: Yes, it is also made for its fragrance,
so that people will smell it
and come and buy from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, לְרֵיחָא נָמֵי הוּא דַּעֲבִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 37
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the scent is intended for smelling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Store spices are only merchandise, not meant to be smelled
steps.terutzMaskana: The perfumer wants his scent smelled to attract customers, so it is made for fragrance
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle survives: what matters is whether the smell itself is meant to be smelled, even if the reason is commercial.

steps.title: Smelling a scent outside a city
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a scent smelled outside a city gets no ברכה if most residents are גוים, and gets a ברכה if most are Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if someone was walking outside a city and smelled a scent, and most of the people there are גוים, he does not make a ברכה. If most are Jews, he makes a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a smell of unknown source. We follow the majority of the town to decide its purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we do not know who burned the spices, we follow the majority of the residents. גוים usually burned incense for עבודה זרה, which gets no ברכה. Jews would usually burn it for fragrance, so a ברכה is made.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If one was walking outside a city
and smelled a scent,
if most are gentiles, he does not make a blessing;
if most are Jews, he makes a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ חוּץ לַכְּרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about a scent whose purpose is unknown
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Follow the majority of residents: mostly גוים means no ברכה, mostly Jews means a ברכה

steps.title: רבי יוסי: even in a Jewish majority there is no ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that even where most residents are Jews there is no ברכה, because some Jewish women burn incense for כשפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: even if most are Jews, he still does not make a ברכה, because Jewish women burn incense for כשפים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the first opinion of the ברייתא. He holds there is no ברכה even in a mostly Jewish town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי worries that the smell may come from incense burned for כשפים, which is not for fragrance. So we cannot assume it is a smell meant for enjoying.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ רוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל — נָמֵי אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ,
phrases.english: Even if most are Jews, he also does not make a blessing,
because the daughters of Israel
burn incense for witchcraft.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the second half of the ברייתא in step 39
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ברכה even in a Jewish-majority town, because of incense for כשפים

steps.title: Do all of them burn incense for witchcraft?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יוסי's reasoning: surely not all Jewish women use incense for כשפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do all of them burn incense for כשפים?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's reason. Only some women do this, so how can it override a Jewish majority?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only a minority burns incense for כשפים, then most incense would still be for fragrance. Following the majority should then require a ברכה, so רבי יוסי's reason seems too weak.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a sharp rhetorical question)

phrases.english: Do they all burn incense for witchcraft?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ לִכְשָׁפִים מְקַטְּרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only a minority does this, so the majority should still be burning incense for fragrance

steps.title: Two minorities make a majority
steps.stepSummary: A minority burns incense for כשפים and another minority burns it to perfume clothing. Together they form a majority that is not for smelling, so there is no ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a minority who burn it for כשפים, and another minority who burn it to perfume clothes. So it turns out that most of it is not made for smelling, and wherever most is not made for smelling, there is no ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי's view. It adds a second group of users, and the two groups together become a majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Perfuming clothes is for the clothes, not for a person to enjoy the smell in the air. Adding this minority to the כשפים minority makes most incense 'not for fragrance'. That fits our principle that such a scent gets no ברכה.
steps.whatToRemember: A ברכה on a smell depends on whether the smell is made to be smelled. A perfume shop counts because the smell draws customers. For an unknown smell we follow the majority, and per רבי יוסי two minorities that are not for fragrance add up to a majority, so there is no ברכה.
steps.confusionAlert: Perfuming clothes does use the scent, but it is meant for the garments, not for smelling in the air. That is why it counts on the 'not for fragrance' side.

phrases.english: There is a minority for witchcraft,
and another minority to perfume garments.
It turns out the majority is not done for fragrance,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל רוּבָּא דְּלָאו לְרֵיחָא עֲבִיד לָא מְבָרֵךְ.
phrases.english: and wherever the majority is not done for fragrance, one does not make a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵה לַהּ מִיעוּטָא לִכְשָׁפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 41 and defends רבי יוסי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining two minorities into a majority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a small minority uses incense for כשפים, so most is for fragrance
steps.terutzMaskana: כשפים plus perfuming clothes together form a majority not for fragrance, so there is no ברכה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Where most incense is not made for smelling, no ברכה is made

steps.title: In טבריא and ציפורי, street scents are assumed to be for perfuming clothes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן rules that one who smells a scent in טבריא on ערב שבת, or in ציפורי on מוצאי שבת, does not make a ברכה, because the scent is assumed to be for perfuming clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone walks in טבריא on Friday afternoons, or in ציפורי on Saturday nights, and smells a nice scent, he does not make a ברכה. The reason is that we assume the scent was made to perfume clothes, not for people to smell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case that follows the same rule as the last few steps: no ברכה on a scent that was not made for smelling. Here the place and the time tell us what the scent is for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 42 the reason for no ברכה was that most incense is used for other purposes. Here רבי יוחנן applies the same idea to a set time and place. In טבריא people perfumed their clothes before שבת, and in ציפורי they did it after שבת, so we assume that a scent smelled then is for clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday afternoons, the time just before שבת
Saturday nights, right after שבת ends
טבריא and ציפורי, two cities in the Galilee
Its presumption: what we assume to be true when we do not know for sure
To perfume clothes or garments with incense smoke

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a local custom can create a חזקה that decides the הלכה. We do not have to know where this particular scent came from, because the common practice tells us what it is for.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cities. טבריא is Friday (before שבת) and ציפורי is Saturday night (after שבת). Each city had its own custom about when to perfume clothes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: The original source of the ruling

phrases.english: One who walks on Friday afternoons in Tiberias
or on Saturday nights in Tzippori
and smelled a scent does not make a blessing,
because the presumption is that it was not made
phrases.notes: חזקה: what we assume based on what usually happens

phrases.english: except to perfume clothes with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle of step 42 (no ברכה on a scent not made for smelling) to a specific time and place based on local custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scent smelled in טבריא on ערב שבת or in ציפורי on מוצאי שבת gets no ברכה, because it is assumed to be for perfuming clothes.

steps.title: Choosing to smell idolatrous incense is a sin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who walks through a marketplace of עבודה זרה and chooses to enjoy the smell of its incense is a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If someone was walking through a marketplace of עבודה זרה and he chose to enjoy the smell, he is a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on a related topic. Here the question is not whether to make a ברכה. It is whether a person may enjoy the smell at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things connected to עבודה זרה are forbidden to benefit from, and smelling is a kind of benefit. The key word is נתרצה, meaning he wanted to smell it. A person who just walks by and cannot avoid the smell is not called a sinner here. Only one who chooses to enjoy it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught. This introduces a ברייתא
Idol worship. Here it refers to idolatrous incense burned in the marketplace
He was willing or wanted. He chose on purpose to enjoy the smell

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say that anyone who walks through and smells it is a sinner. The word נתרצה limits it to one who wants to enjoy the smell.
steps.whatToRemember: So far we have three rules about scents. (1) A scent not made for smelling gets no ברכה. (2) A local custom, such as perfuming clothes in טבריא and ציפורי, makes us assume a scent is not for smelling. (3) Choosing to enjoy the incense of עבודה זרה is not only without a ברכה, it is a sin.
